newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds rise to strong gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bunds rise to strong gains in late trade.

text.p: German Bunds rose to strong gains in late trade on Thursday, boosted by gains in the U.S. debt market amid short-covering ahead of the U.S. December unemployment report due on Friday.

March Bund futures rose as high as 100.31, up 42 basis points from Wednesday's close, and dealers said they could imagine further gains before the end of the session if the market breached key resistance around 100.30.
Dealers said Bunds were boosted by benign inflation data from the U.S. which cooled speculation of an imminent U.S. credit tightening.
Bunds showed little reaction to German 1996 GDP data and December unemployment figures released earlier on Thursday.

GDP growth in 1996 slowed to 1.4 percent last year according to provisional data, down from 1.9 percent in 1995, and the statistics office said the economy stagnated in the final quarter with virtually no growth from the third quarter.

Meanwhile German unemployment rose 48,000 to a seasonally-adjusted 4.156 million in December, a new post-war record that topped the prior level of 4.1 million in November, the Federal Labour Office said.
Financial markets took heart from news that the core producer price (PPI) rate, which excludes fuel and food, rose only 0.1 percent in December, in line with forecasts.
That outweighed the stronger-than-expected 0.5 percent rise in the headline PPI rate.
Bunds were also buoyed by U.S. November wholesale inventories which rose 0.1 percent, below forecasts for a 0.2 percent rise.
"We're focusing mainly on U.S. data, the German data today were all about as expected," one dealer said.

On an unadjusted basis, some 4.148 million were unemployed, below the peak of 4.27 million in February 1996. Federal Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said he could not rule out the unadjusted figure soon reaching 4.5 million.
